lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: Pluto, we cannot live next door to Menippus here. The man is a dog. Either move him somewhere else, or we are moving to another district.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: What exactly is he doing to you? He is just as dead as you are.

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: Whenever we cry and groan over what we left upstairs — Midas here over his gold, Sardanapalus over all his luxury, and I, Croesus, over my treasuries — he laughs at us. He insults us. Calls us slaves and garbage. Sometimes he starts singing and drowns out our lamentations. In short, he is a nuisance.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Entirely, Pluto. I hate them. They are vulgar, disastrous people. It was not enough for them to live badly; they have to go on doing it dead. They still remember all that stuff up there and cling to it. So yes, I enjoy annoying them.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: You should not. They are grieving real losses. Not small ones.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Pluto, are you being stupid too? Are you voting with their groans now?

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Not at all. I simply do not want a civil war in the building.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well then, worst of all Lydians, Phrygians, and Assyrians, understand this: I am not stopping. Wherever you go, I will follow — annoying you, singing at you, laughing at you.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No. Abuse was what you did: demanding to be worshipped, living off free men like toys, and never once thinking about death. So now you can howl, having been relieved of the whole inventory.

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: Such a large inventory, gods. So many great possessions.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Excellent. Keep that up. You do the wailing; I will accompany you, over and over, with Know thyself. It is exactly the hymn those noises deserve.
